findings.claim: The asbestos must be safely removed by a licensed contractor before any other demolition work takes place.
findings.truth: Whether asbestos work needs a licensed contractor is decided by the risk and the legal criteria. Most higher-risk work needs a licence, but some work is non-licensed or notifiable non-licensed work.
findings.evidence: HSE, Licensable work with asbestos, and Non-licensed work with asbestos (fetched 2026-09-04).

findings.claim: On completion, the client receives an operation and maintenance manual required under CDM Regulations.
findings.truth: CDM 2015 requires a health and safety file only for projects involving more than one contractor; it assigns the file to the principal designer or, in some cases, principal contractor. The specification instead says an operation and maintenance manual is given at completion in accordance with relevant CDM sections. Decide whether to remove the legal assertion across the related fields or recast the manual as handover practice.
findings.evidence: HSE L153, Regulation 12 and Appendix 4 (fetched 2026-09-04); specification Unit 1, 1.2.4.

findings.claim: planning authorities are more likely to approve commercial/industrial development on the edge of town than housing
findings.truth: Planning outcomes depend on the proposal, the site and applicable policy. The model answer should credit consideration of the local plan and site constraints, rather than claim a general likelihood of approval.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, When is permission required? (fetched 2026-09-04): development normally needs permission unless a permitted development right applies, and the local planning authority advises on individual planning matters.

summary: Checked all four lessons against the Unit 1 content and assessment requirements. Two surgical corrections are supplied; one CDM issue needs a coordinated editorial decision.
